_what: One public definition per relation type, published in /ns/relation as skos:definition. Drafted by Claude Sonnet from the types' labels and notes, reviewed and approved by Doug Egge on 2026-10-14 ('approve the rest'); the one he rewrote is marked 'by': 'Doug Egge'. The drafted wording is AI-written and excluded from the copyright claim; which types exist and what each joins are his.

spoke_to.definition: That one spoke to another, as the narrator tells it: "Isaac said to Abraham" (Gen 22:7). The speech turn is its evidence; what was said is the turn's content, not this relation.
spoke_to.by: drafted by Claude Opus, 2026-10-20, from the approved recommendation (G1, the 1.2.0 inventory)

states.definition: A statement one clause of the text makes, its subject doing to its object what the verb says: "God loved the world" (John 3:16). The verb is carried with the claim as the verse renders it, with its grammar, the force it is said with and the kind of act it names. Only a statement made outright, by a verb whose form says it happened, is asserted; a command, promise, prediction or purpose is described and never stated. The plain triple carries no verb (every statement uses this one type): read the claim, whose claim:verb and claim:modality say what was said and how.
states.by: drafted by Claude Opus, 2026-10-19, for Doug's review with the 1.2.0 inventory

deity_of.definition: A divine being is called the God of a person or people, as in the text's formula "the God of" a patriarch or of Israel; it is a relationship the text states and not an identification of the two.
deity_of.by: drafted by Claude Sonnet, approved by Doug Egge

self_designated_as.definition: A person or being applies a title to himself in his own speech, as against a title that the narrator or another speaker gives him; it records who said the words and not what follows from them.
self_designated_as.by: drafted by Claude Sonnet, approved by Doug Egge

spoken_of_as.definition: The text applies the name or nature of one person or being to another; the edge says only that a particular verse says so, and it is not a claim that the two are the same.
spoken_of_as.by: drafted by Claude Sonnet, approved by Doug Egge

quoted.definition: A speaker or writing takes up the words of another speaker or writing; the target is the person the text credits with the words, not the book they are found in.
quoted.by: drafted by Claude Sonnet, approved by Doug Egge

named_with.definition: The text names the two together in a single formula or sentence; the edge records the joint naming and does not say how the two are related.
named_with.by: drafted by Claude Sonnet, approved by Doug Egge

distinguished_from.definition: The text sets the two apart, for example when a speaker contrasts himself with another; it records the statement and does not settle what the contrast means.
distinguished_from.by: drafted by Claude Sonnet, approved by Doug Egge

put_away.definition: A person or group sends another away to end a marriage, in the text's own word and not in a later legal term such as divorce.
put_away.by: drafted by Claude Sonnet, approved by Doug Egge

accused.definition: A person or group lays a charge against another person or group; it is the complaint made, not a plot against someone and not the verdict.
accused.by: drafted by Claude Sonnet, approved by Doug Egge

charged.definition: A person, being or group lays a binding instruction on another, stronger than a request.
charged.by: drafted by Claude Sonnet, approved by Doug Egge

besought.definition: A person or group entreats another where the text marks the act as a petition; the polite "please" of ordinary speech is not recorded.
besought.by: drafted by Claude Sonnet, approved by Doug Egge

rebuked.definition: A person, being or group reproves another in an episode the narrative reports; a letter that itself delivers a reproof, without reporting a confrontation, does not make an edge to its readers.
rebuked.by: drafted by Claude Sonnet, approved by Doug Egge

warned.definition: A person, being or group gives another notice of danger or of a consequence to come.
warned.by: drafted by Claude Sonnet, approved by Doug Egge

told.definition: A person, being or group gives a parable, dream or vision, the one the figure belongs to; it is not the one who wrote it down.
told.by: drafted by Claude Sonnet, approved by Doug Egge

explained.definition: A person, being or group gives the interpretation of a parable, dream or vision; it is kept apart from telling because the two are often different people.
explained.by: drafted by Claude Sonnet, approved by Doug Egge

sent.definition: A person, being or group sends another person, being, group or creature, where the text narrates the sending.
sent.by: drafted by Claude Sonnet, approved by Doug Egge

assumed_form_of.definition: A temporary form is the form that a person or being took on and later set aside, where the text narrates the taking; the form is the source and the one who took it is the target.
assumed_form_of.by: drafted by Claude Sonnet, approved by Doug Egge

appeared_to.definition: A being, person or group appears to a person or group in a visitation the text narrates, without classifying it as a vision, a dream or a bodily appearance.
appeared_to.by: drafted by Claude Sonnet, approved by Doug Egge

party_to.definition: A person, group or being is named by the text as a party to a covenant.
party_to.by: drafted by Claude Sonnet, approved by Doug Egge

token_of.definition: An object, observance, creature or place is named by the text as the sign of a covenant.
token_of.by: drafted by Claude Sonnet, approved by Doug Egge

supersedes.definition: One covenant is said by the text to make an earlier covenant obsolete; it is recorded only where the text says so.
supersedes.by: drafted by Claude Sonnet, approved by Doug Egge

assessed_as.definition: A subject is the doer of a deed that the text itself evaluates, such as the verdict pronounced on a reign or on a part of creation; the evaluation is the text's own and not a reader's.
assessed_as.by: drafted by Claude Sonnet, approved by Doug Egge

described_as.definition: A subject is said by the text to be a certain way: an age, a state, a trait, a role or a verdict on the subject itself, as distinct from a deed that is evaluated.
described_as.by: drafted by Claude Sonnet, approved by Doug Egge

titled.definition: A person or being is called by a title that the text gives; the title is its own entity, kept apart from the creature or object it is built from.
titled.by: drafted by Claude Sonnet, approved by Doug Egge

asserted_by.definition: A claim, verdict, title or saying is vouched for by a named party, or by the writing itself where no speaker is named; it lets two differing claims be held side by side without being joined.
asserted_by.by: drafted by Claude Sonnet, approved by Doug Egge

grounds.definition: One statement is the reason the text gives for another, so that the second rests on the first.
grounds.by: drafted by Claude Sonnet, approved by Doug Egge

conditional_on.definition: A consequence the text states is tied to the condition on which it depends, as in a bargain, a blessing or a warning that begins "if".
conditional_on.by: drafted by Claude Sonnet, approved by Doug Egge

recounts.definition: A telling is one account of an event or of another telling, so that two writings can describe the same thing without being merged into one voice.
recounts.by: drafted by Claude Sonnet, approved by Doug Egge

incited.definition: One party moves another to act, in the sense of causing someone to take an action; the action itself is carried by what the one moved then does.
incited.by: drafted by Claude Sonnet, approved by Doug Egge

gave.definition: A person, being or group transfers something to another; the edge records the giving and not what the gift came to mean.
gave.by: drafted by Claude Sonnet, approved by Doug Egge

took.definition: A person, being or group takes something from another or from its place; the counterpart of giving.
took.by: drafted by Claude Sonnet, approved by Doug Egge

ate.definition: A person, being, group or creature eats something, where the text records the eating.
ate.by: drafted by Claude Sonnet, approved by Doug Egge

heard.definition: A person, being or group hears a speech, a cry or a report, where the text records the hearing.
heard.by: drafted by Claude Sonnet, approved by Doug Egge

answered.definition: One speech replies to another, or a person replies to a speech or a person; where the text has a speaker answer the previous speech, the reply is to what was said and not only to the one who said it.
answered.by: drafted by Claude Sonnet, approved by Doug Egge

named.definition: A person, being or group gives a name to someone or something, or changes an existing name, where the text says who did the naming.
named.by: drafted by Claude Sonnet, approved by Doug Egge

destroyed.definition: A person, being or group destroys a place, people, thing or creature, where the text says so.
destroyed.by: drafted by Claude Sonnet, approved by Doug Egge

issues_from.definition: One thing comes out of another as its source; it is origin and not containment, and a river that goes out of a place is not a part of it.
issues_from.by: drafted by Claude Sonnet, approved by Doug Egge

ascribed_to.definition: A writing carries a superscription naming a person or group; the edge records the ascription as it is printed and does not say whether it means authorship, dedication or subject.
ascribed_to.by: drafted by Claude Sonnet, approved by Doug Egge

part_of.definition: One unit of the text lies inside a larger unit, such as a saying within a psalm or a passage within a longer passage; the relation is containment and is passed on through each level.
part_of.by: drafted by Claude Sonnet, approved by Doug Egge

spoken_in.definition: A kind of message is spoken within a pattern, concept, event or passage; it is supported by the verses the message and the other node share, and not by the names sounding alike.
spoken_in.by: drafted by Claude Sonnet, approved by Doug Egge

specializes.definition: One form is a narrower form of a broader form; both are forms and neither is an occurrence, and the grouping is the graph's own and not a statement of the text.
specializes.by: drafted by Claude Sonnet, approved by Doug Egge

instance_of.definition: A passage, saying, event or group is one case of a shape that several passages share; the shape is the graph's grouping and not a claim that the writers intended one.
instance_of.by: drafted by Claude Sonnet, approved by Doug Egge

re_enacts.definition: A later account is told so as to re-enact an earlier one; the grade of the edge says whether the text states it, a quotation carries it, or a reader's correspondence alone supports it.
re_enacts.by: drafted by Claude Sonnet, approved by Doug Egge

takes_up.definition: A later account quotes, summarises or gathers the words given in an earlier one; the pairs of words are the evidence and no likeness between persons is claimed.
takes_up.by: drafted by Claude Sonnet, approved by Doug Egge

same_steps_as.definition: Two accounts have the same sequence of steps, each step quoted from both texts; the edge makes no claim that either was told with the other in mind.
same_steps_as.by: drafted by Claude Sonnet, approved by Doug Egge

possibly_same_as.definition: Two person records that the text never joins may, in a reader's view, be one person; this is not an identity, each record keeps its own verses, and the evidence is given on both sides.
possibly_same_as.by: drafted by Claude Sonnet, approved by Doug Egge

occasion_of.definition: An event is an occasion of a significant number, being a time the text counts as that span; the edge is cited to the verse that counts it and claims no meaning for the number.
occasion_of.by: drafted by Claude Sonnet, approved by Doug Egge

composed_of.definition: A phrase is built from the words of a term; this is a fact about the wording only and does not say that the phrase is a kind of that thing.
composed_of.by: drafted by Claude Sonnet, approved by Doug Egge

draws_on.definition: A title, saying or image is built on another image, person, place, being or text; this is a claim about wording and not about what the image means.
draws_on.by: drafted by Claude Sonnet, approved by Doug Egge

drawn_from.definition: A word used as an image is joined to the tangible thing of the same name, where the graph holds one; the two share a word and are not one node.
drawn_from.by: drafted by Claude Sonnet, approved by Doug Egge

likened_to.definition: The text marks a comparison in which the first is compared to the second, the thing described being the source and the image the target.
likened_to.by: drafted by Claude Sonnet, approved by Doug Egge

made.definition: A person, group or being fashions or creates something, where the text names the maker; commissioning the work is a separate relation.
made.by: drafted by Claude Sonnet, approved by Doug Egge

commanded_the_making_of.definition: A person or being commands that something be made, which is kept apart from the one who does the making.
commanded_the_making_of.by: drafted by Claude Sonnet, approved by Doug Egge

wore.definition: A person or group wears a garment or piece of dress the text puts on them; it is not the same as carrying the garment and says nothing of who had the right to wear it.
wore.by: drafted by Claude Sonnet, approved by Doug Egge

kept_at.definition: An object, concept or creature is kept at a place; an object that moves can have several such places, each with its own citation.
kept_at.by: drafted by Claude Sonnet, approved by Doug Egge

carried.definition: A person or group bears or transports an object, concept or creature.
carried.by: drafted by Claude Sonnet, approved by Doug Egge

signifies.definition: The text states outright what a thing stands for; it records the key the text gives and not a reader's decision about what something means, and it does not carry over to other uses of the same word.
signifies.by: drafted by Claude Sonnet, approved by Doug Egge

bought.definition: A person or group buys a place, object or thing, in a purchase the text records.
bought.by: drafted by Claude Sonnet, approved by Doug Egge

built.definition: A person, group or being raises a place or structure, where the text says who built it.
built.by: drafted by Claude Sonnet, approved by Doug Egge

repaired.definition: A person or group repairs a place or structure; it is kept apart from building because the text distinguishes the two.
repaired.by: drafted by Claude Sonnet, approved by Doug Egge

ruler_of.definition: A person holds a district office over a place or group; it is a ruling office and not a throne, and one district may have more than one such officer.
ruler_of.by: drafted by Claude Sonnet, approved by Doug Egge

instituted.definition: A person or being establishes an observance, where the text names who established it.
instituted.by: drafted by Claude Sonnet, approved by Doug Egge

observed.definition: A person or group keeps an observance on an occasion the text records.
observed.by: drafted by Claude Sonnet, approved by Doug Egge

father_of.definition: A person is the father of another, as a direct generation; a wider descent is recorded as ancestry instead.
father_of.by: drafted by Claude Sonnet, approved by Doug Egge

mother_of.definition: A person is the mother of another, as a direct generation.
mother_of.by: drafted by Claude Sonnet, approved by Doug Egge

sibling_of.definition: Two people are siblings, full or unspecified; the relation reads the same from either side.
sibling_of.by: drafted by Claude Sonnet, approved by Doug Egge

half_sibling_of.definition: Two people share one parent, where the text is explicit about it; the relation reads the same from either side.
half_sibling_of.by: drafted by Claude Sonnet, approved by Doug Egge

ancestor_of.definition: A person or group is an ancestor of another across more than one generation, or without the intervening generations being given, including a people traced to a named ancestor.
ancestor_of.by: drafted by Claude Sonnet, approved by Doug Egge

uncle_of.definition: A person is the uncle or aunt of another, recorded where the text states it and not where it follows from two named parents and a sibling.
uncle_of.by: drafted by Claude Sonnet, approved by Doug Egge

cousin_of.definition: Two people are cousins, recorded only where the text itself says so; the relation reads the same from either side.
cousin_of.by: drafted by Claude Sonnet, approved by Doug Egge

adoptive_parent_of.definition: A person who becomes a parent of another through a willful, formal process of adoption.

spouse_of.definition: Two people are married to each other; the relation reads the same from either side.
spouse_of.by: drafted by Claude Sonnet, approved by Doug Egge

concubine_of.definition: A woman is a concubine of a man, a status the text distinguishes from marriage; the concubine is the source and the man the target.
concubine_of.by: drafted by Claude Sonnet, approved by Doug Egge

betrothed_to.definition: Two people are betrothed to each other before marriage; the relation reads the same from either side.
betrothed_to.by: drafted by Claude Sonnet, approved by Doug Egge

predecessor_of.definition: A person held an office, such as king, high priest or judge, and another held it next; the direction always runs from the earlier holder to the later.
predecessor_of.by: drafted by Claude Sonnet, approved by Doug Egge

co_regent_with.definition: Two people reigned jointly; the relation reads the same from either side.
co_regent_with.by: drafted by Claude Sonnet, approved by Doug Egge

appointed.definition: A person, group or being places a person or group in an office or command.
appointed.by: drafted by Claude Sonnet, approved by Doug Egge

offered.definition: A person or group offers a person, creature or object as a sacrifice; it records the act the text names and not whether the offering was carried through.
offered.by: drafted by Claude Sonnet, approved by Doug Egge

speaks_of.definition: A statement, title, image or verdict makes a claim about the thing it names; the statement is the source with the verse behind it, and nothing runs the other way.
speaks_of.by: drafted by Claude Sonnet, approved by Doug Egge

came_upon.definition: The Spirit or another being comes upon a person or group, as the text puts it; the edge says the verse reports this and does not say what the coming produced or how long it lasted.
came_upon.by: drafted by Claude Sonnet, approved by Doug Egge

anointed.definition: A person or group anoints a person, as the text records it; a body of people can confer the office as well as a prophet.
anointed.by: drafted by Claude Sonnet, approved by Doug Egge

deposed.definition: A person is removed from power by another.
deposed.by: drafted by Claude Sonnet, approved by Doug Egge

servant_of.definition: A person, group or concept serves a person, group or being; the relation covers officials, armour-bearers, stewards and slaves alike, since the text rarely separates them.
servant_of.by: drafted by Claude Sonnet, approved by Doug Egge

commander_of.definition: A person commanded the army of another.
commander_of.by: drafted by Claude Sonnet, approved by Doug Egge

counselor_of.by: drafted by Claude Sonnet, approved by Doug Egge

prophet_to.definition: A person speaks as a prophet to a person or group, confronting them with a message.
prophet_to.by: drafted by Claude Sonnet, approved by Doug Egge

mentor_of.definition: A person was the master or mentor of another, who was the disciple.
mentor_of.by: drafted by Claude Sonnet, approved by Doug Egge

blessed.definition: A being, person or group pronounces a formal and consequential blessing on a person or group, not a casual greeting.
blessed.by: drafted by Claude Sonnet, approved by Doug Egge

cursed.definition: A person or being pronounces a curse on a person, group, place, creature, object or being.
cursed.by: drafted by Claude Sonnet, approved by Doug Egge

baptized.definition: A person or being baptizes a person or group.
baptized.by: drafted by Claude Sonnet, approved by Doug Egge

healed.definition: A person or being heals, casts out a spirit from, or raises from the dead, a person or group the text names or clearly picks out.
healed.by: drafted by Claude Sonnet, approved by Doug Egge

ministered_to.definition: A person, group or being teaches or ministers to another in a substantial personal encounter that is neither a healing nor an ongoing discipleship.
ministered_to.by: drafted by Claude Sonnet, approved by Doug Egge

ally_of.definition: Two parties were allied politically or militarily; the relation reads the same from either side and is not a mere friendship.
ally_of.by: drafted by Claude Sonnet, approved by Doug Egge

friend_of.definition: Two people were close friends; the relation reads the same from either side.
friend_of.by: drafted by Claude Sonnet, approved by Doug Egge

companion_of.definition: Two people travelled or worked together; the relation reads the same from either side.
companion_of.by: drafted by Claude Sonnet, approved by Doug Egge

persecuted.definition: A person or group pursued another with sustained harm, from a position of power over them, and not by a single act of violence.
persecuted.by: drafted by Claude Sonnet, approved by Doug Egge

enemy_of.definition: Two parties were declared or lasting enemies where neither is clearly the aggressor; the relation reads the same from either side.
enemy_of.by: drafted by Claude Sonnet, approved by Doug Egge

contrary_to.definition: The text sets two things against each other, by saying they are contrary or by building the contrast into its structure; the opposition is the text's and not a reader's, and tensions the text leaves standing are not recorded.
contrary_to.by: drafted by Claude Sonnet, approved by Doug Egge

conspired_against.definition: A person, group or being plots against a person or group.
conspired_against.by: drafted by Claude Sonnet, approved by Doug Egge

betrayed.definition: A person or group betrays another person or group.
betrayed.by: drafted by Claude Sonnet, approved by Doug Egge

killed.definition: A person, group or being kills a person, group or creature, including by ordering the death.
killed.by: drafted by Claude Sonnet, approved by Doug Egge

attacked.definition: A person, group or being attacks or makes war on a person or group.
attacked.by: drafted by Claude Sonnet, approved by Doug Egge

deceived.definition: A person, group, being or creature deceives a person, group or being.
deceived.by: drafted by Claude Sonnet, approved by Doug Egge

cast_into.definition: A person or group is put into a place or object against their will and kept there; the source is the one who ends up inside and not the one who threw them.
cast_into.by: drafted by Claude Sonnet, approved by Doug Egge

imprisoned.definition: A person or group holds another person, group or concept in captivity.
imprisoned.by: drafted by Claude Sonnet, approved by Doug Egge

founded.definition: A person founded a place, or is called the father of a town in the text's idiom, which is usually read as its founder or chief ancestor; the words of the phrase are quoted so that a reader can weigh the reading.
founded.by: drafted by Claude Sonnet, approved by Doug Egge

born_at.definition: A person was born at a place, recorded only where the text says born and not merely present.
born_at.by: drafted by Claude Sonnet, approved by Doug Egge

died_at.definition: A person died at a place.
died_at.by: drafted by Claude Sonnet, approved by Doug Egge

buried_at.definition: A person was buried at a place or object.
buried_at.by: drafted by Claude Sonnet, approved by Doug Egge

dwelt_at.definition: A person or group lived at a place, a settled residence the text establishes and not a single visit.
dwelt_at.by: drafted by Claude Sonnet, approved by Doug Egge

stationed_at.definition: A being or creature is posted at a place or object and left there; it records the placement and not residence or purpose.
stationed_at.by: drafted by Claude Sonnet, approved by Doug Egge

reigned_over.definition: A person reigned over a realm or a people; the realm and the seat of government are separate facts.
reigned_over.by: drafted by Claude Sonnet, approved by Doug Egge

ruled_from.definition: A person ruled from a place that was the seat of the rule.
ruled_from.by: drafted by Claude Sonnet, approved by Doug Egge

traveled_to.definition: A person or group went to a place on a journey the narrative marks; it is deliberately a weak tie.
traveled_to.by: drafted by Claude Sonnet, approved by Doug Egge

member_of.definition: A person or concept belonged to a group, recorded only where the text places them in it.
member_of.by: drafted by Claude Sonnet, approved by Doug Egge

led.definition: A person, being, group or concept leads a person or group, including the leading of one person by God.
led.by: drafted by Claude Sonnet, approved by Doug Egge

present_with.definition: A being, person, group or concept is with a person, group, being or concept, where the text states the presence in so many words.
present_with.by: drafted by Claude Sonnet, approved by Doug Egge

descended_from_person.definition: A tribe or nation descends from the person it is named for, as the text explains the origin of a people; the person and the people remain separate nodes.
descended_from_person.by: drafted by Claude Sonnet, approved by Doug Egge

fought.definition: A person or group made war on a person or group, where either side may be a person or a people.
fought.by: drafted by Claude Sonnet, approved by Doug Egge

conquered.definition: A person or group subjugated another with a lasting outcome, as distinct from a single battle.
conquered.by: drafted by Claude Sonnet, approved by Doug Egge

wrote_to.definition: A person wrote to a congregation, taken from the address of the letter itself; the target is the group and not the town where it met.
wrote_to.by: drafted by Claude Sonnet, approved by Doug Egge

wrote_letter_to.definition: A person wrote to another person, taken from the address of the letter itself.
wrote_letter_to.by: drafted by Claude Sonnet, approved by Doug Egge

based_at.definition: A group is centred on a place, so that a church, household or tribe is a group with a location and not a synonym for the place.
based_at.by: drafted by Claude Sonnet, approved by Doug Egge

located_in.definition: A place or object lies within a larger place.
located_in.by: drafted by Claude Sonnet, approved by Doug Egge

judged.definition: A person, group or being passes judgment on a person or group, in a formal legal proceeding or a pronounced verdict.
judged.by: drafted by Claude Sonnet, approved by Doug Egge

aspect_of.definition: A concept or pattern is one facet of a broader idea, joined to it and not merged into it; the grouping is the map's and not the text's, and each aspect is described by the passages it cites.
aspect_of.by: drafted by Claude Sonnet, approved by Doug Egge

in_theme.definition: A concept, observance, event or saying is a core concept of a major theme; the grouping is a reader's map of the text, supported by the passages cited.
in_theme.by: drafted by Claude Sonnet, approved by Doug Egge
